ai.title: Context pruner includes non-blacklisted spawnagents results
ai.summary: The context pruner now captures and summarizes tool results from `spawn_agents` calls, excluding a defined blacklist of utility agents like `file-picker` and `code-searcher`. This change ensures that outputs from substantive spawned agents are preserved in the summarized context, while noisy or redundant results from helper agents are filtered out. The mechanism involves iterating through `spawn_agents` results, filtering by `agentType` against `SPAWN_AGENTS_OUTPUT_BLACKLIST`, stripping `<think>` tags, and truncating long outputs to `ASSISTANT_MESSAGE_LIMIT`. This affects `agents/context-pruner.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant summarizes a long conversation, it now keeps the results that count: the outputs produced by the helper programs it sends out to do work. It skips the noisy side outputs from simple utility programs like file finders and code searchers, so the recap stays clean and useful. If you ever look at one of these summaries, you'll see real answers from the substantive helpers collected into a section labeled agent results, instead of one big tangle of everything the assistant asked for.

ai.title: Max mode swaps reviewer-editor-gpt-5 for code-reviewer-multi-prompt
ai.summary: Max mode agent configuration now uses `code-reviewer-multi-prompt` instead of `reviewer-editor-gpt-5` in `agents/base2/base2.ts`. The new `code-reviewer-multi-prompt` agent spawns multiple `code-reviewer` instances with distinct focus prompts (e.g., security, performance) and merges their outputs into a single structured review. This change affects only the internal agent orchestration for max-mode sessions.

eli5.text: If you turn on Max mode, the review step now runs several specialized code checkers at once instead of reusing the same assistant used for writing. Each checker examines the code for a particular concern like security or speed, and you see their combined findings in a single report. The change is live for Max mode sessions today.

ai.title: Remove agent status footer from AgentBlockGrid
ai.summary: Removed `getAgentStatusSummary` and the status footer from `AgentBlockGrid` in `cli/src/components/blocks/agent-block-grid.tsx`. The footer displayed running, failed, and completed agent counts based on `streamingAgents` and block status. This simplifies the grid by removing the `streamingAgents` prop and theme dependencies for the footer.

eli5.text: If you run the CLI tool today, you will no longer see a small status line at the bottom of the agent grid that used to read things like '3 agents running' or '2 failed, 1 completed'. The change only affects the command-line interface grid that shows your helper agents, and nothing else in the program changes.

ai.title: Remove best-of-n reviewer and base2 agents
ai.summary: Deleted `agents/reviewer/best-of-n` and `agents/base2` directories, removing `code-reviewer-best-of-n`, `code-reviewer-implementor`, `code-reviewer-selector`, and `base2-with-planner-pro` agent definitions. `decomposing-thinker` moved to `.agents-graveyard` with updated relative imports. This reduces the agent surface area and removes complex orchestration logic for code review and planning.

eli5.text: The system dropped two of its more complex multi-step review helpers: one that ran several reviewers and picked the best result, and a separate planning helper that coordinated multiple agent types. If you're a user, you would not notice these directly, but you might see a different review helper name appear in places that previously referenced them, and any workflows relying on the now-removed helpers will need to be swapped to the replacement review helper.

ai.title: Rename .agents-graveyard to agents-graveyard
ai.summary: Directory rename. Dot-prefixed path removed. Internal repo structure updated. No code logic changes.

eli5.text: The project renamed an internal folder that held retired, unused helper files from a name starting with a dot to one without the dot. Nothing users or the live workflow touch changed, those files were already set aside, so most people will notice nothing at all, but anyone digging into the project's folder structure would see those old files moved to a slightly different path.

ai.title: Update max agent prompts to use code-reviewer-multi-prompt
ai.summary: The max mode prompts in `agents/base2/base2.ts` now reference `code-reviewer-multi-prompt` instead of `reviewer-editor-gpt-5` for code review tasks. This aligns the agent's review step with the updated multi-prompt reviewer architecture. The change ensures the agent spawns the correct reviewer agent for max mode operations.

eli5.text: When one of these agents works in its highest-power mode, it now hires a different code reviewer to check its work. Previously it used an older reviewer; now it uses the newer multi-prompt reviewer. If you watched the agent in action you'd notice it spawning a reviewer with a new name, but the rest of how it behaves stays the same.

eli5.text: When you ask the code-review assistant to look at a change, it can now accept several short review instructions in a single message. Those instructions can now specifically name which part of the code to examine, like the frontend or backend, or describe a reviewing angle such as looking for ways to simplify the code or reuse existing pieces. The written guidance for this feature was updated today to show clearer examples of how to supply these review instructions, so anyone configuring the assistant will find it easier to request a focused review.

ai.title: Simplify CLI multi-prompt editor UI
ai.summary: Removed dynamic 'proposals generated' header and per-file hunk counts from `ImplementorGroup` and `CompactFileRow` in `cli/src/components/blocks/implementor-row.tsx`. Added/removed diff bars switched from bright `theme.success`/`theme.error` backgrounds to muted hex colors `#3A5A3A`/`#5A3A3A` with `theme.foreground` text. Layout width calculations updated to exclude hunk text, granting more space for file paths.

eli5.text: Starting today, the on-screen list that shows each draft the assistant is working on looks simpler. The running tally like "2 proposals generated" no longer appears above the file list, each file row no longer shows a separate hunk count, and the green and red change bars next to file names use softer, muted colors instead of bright highlights. If you open the multi-prompt editor you will see more room for each file path to fit on one line and a calmer color scheme, with the same plus/minus numbers still visible inside the bars.

ai.title: Enforce read-only mode and trim history in multi-prompt reviewer
ai.summary: Code reviewer prompts now explicitly forbid tool calls to prevent accidental state modification. Multi-prompt agent strips trailing user messages from history via set_messages before spawning sub-agents. This reduces context noise and ensures sub-agents review only the intended diff scope. Files: agents/reviewer/code-reviewer.ts, agents/reviewer/multi-prompt/code-reviewer-multi-prompt.ts.

eli5.text: When the automated code-review assistant runs in its multi-prompt mode, it now silently removes the trailing back-and-forth messages from its conversation history before spinning up helper reviewers, so each sub-review is scoped to just the code diff under inspection. The main reviewer prompt also now carries an explicit instruction to stay read-only by not invoking any tools, preventing a well-meaning AI from accidentally editing the files it was only supposed to look at. You would notice nothing on the surface today, since these are internal guardrails that keep the review process tidy and safe behind the scenes.

ai.title: Base2 max mode runs typecheck before code review
ai.summary: Base2 agent max mode now sequences typecheck before code-reviewer-multi-prompt. Previous logic ran them in parallel. Change affects agents/base2/base2.ts prompt construction.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to review a large, complex codebase (its so-called "max mode"), it now runs a type check first before having an automated reviewer read over the code, previously both happened at the same time, so the reviewer sometimes saw incomplete or inconsistent code. This only affects the agent's deepest, most thorough analysis pass and makes the review step more reliable. If you triggered this mode, you'd see the type check complete before the reviewer starts its pass. The change is live today for anyone using that mode.

eli5.text: When the multi-prompt code reviewer runs and spawns individual code reviewers inside it, those child reviewers now get visually collapsed (hidden/minimized) in the CLI transcript instead of showing every nested output. This affects anyone running code reviews via the CLI who uses the code-reviewer-multi-prompt agent. If you looked, you'd notice a cleaner transcript with less repetitive review output from the nested agents.

ai.title: Freebuff 1.0.586 ships multi-prompt reviewer and CLI layout
ai.summary: Release 1.0.586 ships a sequence of same-day commits affecting the CLI surface, agent-runtime, and agents packages. Max mode now swaps reviewer-editor-gpt-5 for code-reviewer-multi-prompt, which spawns parallel code-reviewer instances with distinct focus prompts and collapses child blocks in the CLI transcript. The CLI rendering layer gains GridLayout, useGridLayout, block-processor utilities, and sequential message-queue processing, alongside new components like AgentBlockGrid, ToolBlockGroup, and UserErrorBanner. Error handling is hardened via endpoint-aware API messages and dual status/statusCode checks for Claude OAuth errors.
ai.evidence: Commit modifies only cli/release/package.json, changing the version field from 1.0.585 to 1.0.586. The release updates list covers preceding commits in the same-day sequence through 2026-01-18, including reviewer agent swaps, CLI layout refactors, and error-handling fixes.

eli5.text: Freebuff 1.0.586 adds a smarter multi-prompt code reviewer that runs several specialized checks (such as security and performance) at once, then merges the results into one structured review, plus a cleaner, grid-based layout for the command-line interface that shows multiple work branches side by side. The new reviewer replaces the older single-reviewer setup in max mode sessions, explicitly forbids accidental file changes, and sequences a type check before review so findings are more reliable. The command-line interface now processes queued messages one at a time to prevent jumbled or overlapping conversations, adds responsive multi-column layouts that adapt to your terminal width, and includes a new error banner that makes runtime problems easier to read. Upgrading gives you faster, more accurate code reviews with fewer distractions, plus a smoother terminal experience that keeps your work organized and your messages in the correct order.

ai.title: code-reviewer.ts adds think tag directive
ai.summary: Prompt injection in agents/reviewer/code-reviewer.ts instructs the code reviewer agent to use <think></think> tags before generating review output. This change enforces internal reasoning steps prior to providing feedback, aiming to improve the quality of suggestions by forcing the model to process the diff context first. Scope limited to the reviewer agent's system prompt configuration.

eli5.text: When the code review assistant writes feedback, it now has an instruction to silently reason through the changes before producing its public summary. The reasoning itself stays internal and is never shown in the review output. If you look at a review today, you won't see any difference in how the feedback appears; the change only affects how the assistant prepares its response behind the scenes.

ai.title: CLI 1.0.587 release bundles reviewer and context pruning improvements
ai.summary: Version 1.0.587 rolls up the same-day changes that updated max mode to use code-reviewer-multi-prompt instead of reviewer-editor-gpt-5, collapsed nested code-reviewer subagents under their parent in the CLI transcript, added think-tag reasoning directives to the code reviewer system prompt, and extended the context pruner to capture spawn_agents results from non-blacklisted agents. The release bump is confined to cli/release/package.json and does not alter runtime behavior itself; it tags the aggregation of those prior commits.
ai.evidence: cli/release/package.json version field changed from 1.0.586 to 1.0.587. Release notes list user-visible improvements since 1.0.586 including spawn_agents context pruning, code-reviewer-multi-prompt replacing reviewer-editor-gpt-5 in max mode, collapsed nested review agents, and think-tag directives in code-reviewer prompts.

eli5.text: This release improves the built-in code reviewer so it thinks through your changes before giving feedback. The code review agent now pauses to reason over the full diff before writing its summary, which makes its suggestions more accurate and helpful. Upgrading gives you higher-quality reviews that catch more subtle issues by forcing the reviewer to fully process what changed instead of jumping straight to comments.
